143	- **`@gravity-ui/uikit` MUST be installed in every Gravity UI project.** It is
144	  the base component + design-token library every other `@gravity-ui/*` package
145	  builds on; without it components render unstyled. If `package.json` lacks it,
146	  stop and have the user install and configure it first (setup:

152	  and the component's README in `dist/docs`. If still unsure, ask the user
153	  rather than guessing.

155	  match an icon from a screenshot/photo/mock, run `scripts/icon-image-search.sh`

181	  ask the user. See `rules/hallucination-traps.md`.

183	  serves the newest major, which may differ from the installed one and have a
184	  different API. The versioned online fallback is the major-line URL
185	  (`/llms/<pkg>/<major>/llms.txt`); below that, go LOCAL.

188	  UI. Override the full brand token set, on each theme you support.
189	- **Do not override internal markup with `[class*='…']` / ID selectors.**
190	  That's written against one DOM structure and breaks silently when the
191	  component changes. Climb the customization ladder
192	  (global token → component CSS API → narrow flagged hack) before ever
193	  touching structure.

205	  `node_modules/@gravity-ui/uikit/build/docs/guides/theming.md` for the
206	  version-matched file.

208	  spacing scale (`--g-spacing-*`), `Flex`/`Box`, `Row`/`Col`/`Container`
209	  grid, breakpoints, `useLayoutContext`.
210	- `references/icons.md` — finding an icon by image
211	  (`scripts/icon-image-search.sh`) or on gravity-ui.com/icons; the
212	  object-vs-string rendering rule.

214	  commonly invented APIs: typography variants (`header-3..6` don't exist, no
215	  `Heading`), the flex contract (`min-width:0`, who shrinks), theming traps

# Colors ## Palette and series colors Set `data.colors` to choose the chart palette. Series without an explicit color use the palette. Set `series.data[].color` to a CSS color string, such as `'#4da2f1'`, `'rgb(77, 162, 241)'`, or `'blue'`, to override a series color. ## Point colors Set a point's `color` to override its color. For line, area, and area range series, this changes markers and tooltip symbols, leaving the line and fill colors unchanged. Marker color priority is `data[].marker.color`, then `data[].color`, the gradient color at the marker position, and finally the series color. For line and area series, the tooltip symbol uses the same resolved color as the point's marker. ## Gradients [Line](./series-types/line.md), [area](./series-types/area.md), and [area range](./series-types/area-range.md) support gradients in `color`. Area and area range also support them in `fillColor`. Only linear gradients are supported. A gradient contains at least two color stops with offsets in non-decreasing order from `0` to `1`. Stop colors support hex, rgb/rgba, hsl/hsla, and named color formats. ```javascript color: { type: 'linear-gradient', angle: 90, stops: [ {offset: 0, color: '#000000'}, {offset: 1, color: '#f0f0f0'}, ], } ``` The optional `angle` follows the CSS convention: - `0` — bottom to top - `90` — left to right - `180` — top to bottom (default) - `270` — right to left The following example renders a left-to-right gradient line. Select part of the X axis to zoom:
See LinearGradient and GradientStop for the complete configuration. ### Zoom and range slider The gradient uses the full series bounds before zoom or range-slider filtering. Colors at retained points stay the same after zoom, reset, and range-slider changes. The range-slider preview uses the same colors. Resizing recalculates the full-series gradient for the new dimensions; oblique gradients can change color when the aspect ratio changes. This applies to category, linear, datetime, and logarithmic axes, including reversed axes. Neighboring points retained for clipping use the same gradient. Null gaps do not restart it. Category axes can remove categories after filtering or hiding series. If this changes the relative distances between retained categories, a single linear gradient cannot preserve the entire line or fill color field. Markers and tooltip symbols retain their sampled full-series colors in this case. ## Legend colors A discrete legend uses a solid symbol. For a gradient, it takes the color at offset `0.5`. The series guides describe whether the symbol uses the line or fill color. A [continuous legend](./legend.md#continuous-legend) has its own color scale.

# Line series A line series connects points to show how a value changes along an ordered axis. ## When to use Use it for trends over time and comparisons between a few metrics. Keep the X values in their meaningful order; use [scatter](./scatter.md) when points have no sequence. ## Example
## Data Set `type: 'line'`. Each point contains `x` and `y`. For a category axis, use a category name or its zero-based index in `categories`; for a datetime axis, use a timestamp in milliseconds. See [Axis types](../axes/axis-types.md). ## Series options ### Markers Set `marker.enabled: true` to keep point markers visible. Configure their hover radius, border color, and border width through `series.options.line.states.hover.marker`. Hover styles apply to both always-visible and hover-only markers. The normal appearance returns when hover moves to another point or leaves the chart. Set `states.hover.enabled: false` to keep always-visible markers unchanged while retaining hover-only markers. Set `states.hover.marker.enabled: false` to disable both marker hover styles and hover-only markers. Area and area-range series support the same options under their respective series keys.
Use [axis padding](../axes/index.md#axis-padding) to fit markers at free axis limits. ### Line interpolation By default, lines connect points with straight segments. Set `interpolation: {type: 'monotone'}` to draw a smooth curve through the points without introducing new extrema. Order points monotonically by X. Markers, tooltips, and interactions stay attached to the original points.
For a cardinal spline, set `interpolation: {type: 'cardinal', tension: 0.5}`. The `tension` ranges from `0` (default, a loose curve) to `1` (straight segments). Below `1`, the curve can overshoot the data extrema and be clipped at the plot boundary. Both curves preserve `nullMode`: gaps and zero-fills are applied before interpolation. Omit `interpolation` or set `{type: 'linear'}` to restore straight segments. ## Colors The `color` property accepts a solid color or a [gradient](../colors.md#gradients). Gradient bounds include the points that participate in the line. ## Data labels By default, labels appear above their points and shift into the plot when they do not fit. Use `dataLabels.placement` to choose other positions. ### Marker boundary Set `dataLabels.anchor: 'marker-edge'` to measure `padding` from the normal marker's outer bounds, including its shape and border. The default, `anchor: 'center'`, measures padding from the data point coordinates. ```javascript { type: 'line', marker: {enabled: true, radius: 10}, dataLabels: {enabled: true, anchor: 'marker-edge', padding: 5}, } ```
This works with every placement direction, automatic placement, and SVG or HTML labels. Hidden markers use the point coordinates; hover does not move labels. Labels are still shifted into the plot area and use the configured fallback, so overlaps can occur near the edges. Labels render above their series' markers regardless of the anchor. ### Automatic placement Set `placement: 'auto'` to try top, bottom, left, and right in that order. The first position that avoids all line series and already placed labels is used. When labels compete for space, the series listed first in `series.data` wins.
### Fixed positions and fallback An array sets the positions to try, for example `placement: ['bottom', 'top']`. A single entry fixes the position. Use `placementFallback: 'hide'` to hide labels that do not fit; the default `'show'` draws them at the first position anyway: ```javascript { type: 'line', dataLabels: {enabled: true, placement: ['bottom'], placementFallback: 'hide'}, } ``` `allowOverlap: true` permits overlap with other labels; lines are still avoided. Placement works with SVG and HTML labels (`html: true`), and collision checks follow interpolated curves. See LineSeriesDataLabels for the complete configuration. ## API reference LineSeries · ChartSeriesOptions

Set `interpolation: {type: 'monotone'}` to draw a smooth curve through the points without introducing new extrema. Order points monotonically by X. Markers, tooltips, and interactions stay attached to the original points.
For a cardinal spline, set `interpolation: {type: 'cardinal', tension: 0.5}`. The `tension` ranges from `0` (default, a loose curve) to `1` (straight segments).
